passages.title: The Whispering Trees
passages.text: Long ago, the trees of the forest could speak, but only to people who were patient enough to listen. A young woodcutter named Edwin often sat beneath an old oak to eat his lunch. One day, he heard a faint voice warning him that a storm was coming. Although the sky was clear, Edwin decided to trust the tree and hurried home. That night, a terrible storm destroyed half of the village's fields, but Edwin had already brought his goats inside. From then on, the villagers stopped laughing at him for talking to trees.

Children spend at least one day a week outdoors, whatever the weather, building shelters, identifying plants and learning to work in teams. Teachers say that pupils who struggle in the classroom often do well outside, and many become more confident. However, some parents worry about safety and the cost of waterproof clothing.

passages.title: Gina's Diary
passages.text: I've always been scared of heights, so when my friends suggested the treetop adventure trail, I nearly said no. In the end I went, mainly because I didn't want to be the only one left behind. The first bridge was terrifying and my legs were shaking. But by the third platform, I was actually enjoying the view. I'm not saying I've completely got over my fear, but I'm proud I didn't give up.

passages.title: The Lantern Makers
passages.text: Every autumn, the families of Willowmere make paper lanterns for the Festival of Light. The tradition began two hundred years ago, when a lost child was guided home by a line of lanterns hung along the river. Today, around three hundred lanterns are made each year. Children decorate them with drawings of animals, while adults fix the frames, which are made of thin bamboo. Although electric lights would be easier and safer, most villagers insist on real candles, saying that 'a lantern without a flame is just a paper bag'.

You might discover that you like the new girl too. And remember, it's healthy to have more than one close friend.

passages.text: Last Friday, our class spent a night at the Natural History Museum. After the museum closed, a guide took us on a torch-lit tour. The dinosaur skeleton looked much scarier in the dark! passages.text: Many students say a 15-minute break is too short. By the time they've queued for a snack, it's time to go back. One idea is to make lunch shorter and morning break longer, so the day stays the same length.

passages.title: Mira and the Recycling Robot
passages.text: When Mira noticed that her school's recycling bins were always full of the wrong things, she decided to do something about it. With help from the science club, she built a robot that could recognise plastic, paper and metal using a small camera. The robot wasn't always right at first; it once put a banana skin in the paper bin. After a month of improvements, though, it was correct nine times out of ten, and the school asked her to build two more.

passages.title: Why Do Cats Purr?
passages.text: Most people think cats purr only when they are happy, but scientists have found that's not the whole story. Cats also purr when they are hurt, frightened or giving birth. One idea is that purring helps them calm down. Another is that the low sound may even help bones heal faster. Kittens can purr when they are just a few days old, which helps their mother know they are safe and well fed.

The lighthouse keeper, Mrs Ward, said he always seemed to know when a storm was coming, because he would sit by the window and stare at the sea. When Captain died, the village put a small statue of him by the lighthouse door, and tourists still rub his nose for luck.

In a survey at the end, 60% of students said they wanted to continue, while 25% wanted phones back and the rest didn't mind.

passages.text: While clearing out her grandfather's attic, Sofia found an old map of her town drawn in pencil. In one corner, someone had marked an X beside the old oak tree in the park, with the words 'For the next explorer'. Sofia and her cousin dug carefully at the spot and found a tin box. Inside were marbles, a compass and a note from her grandfather, written when he was ten: 'If you found this, you are a true explorer.'

passages.title: Ask Dr Paws: Help, My Dog Hates Baths!
passages.text: Dear Dr Paws, my dog Bean runs away every time I get the bath ready. What can I do? — Mia, 11. | Dear Mia, many dogs feel nervous in the bath because the floor is slippery. Try putting a rubber mat in the bottom. Use warm, not hot, water, and give Bean a treat before, during and after. Keep the first baths very short. Most importantly, stay calm: dogs can tell when you are stressed!

her dog is far too noisy
questions.explain: 'Bean runs away every time I get the bath ready.'

questions.explain: 'Before, during and after.'

notes.never during a bath: Treats during the bath are advised.

questions.q: What is the most important tip?
questions.explain: 'Most importantly, stay calm.'

passages.title: Blog: How I Taught My Puppy to Fetch
passages.text: When we adopted Waffles from the animal shelter, he was scared of almost everything, even his own toys. My aunt, who trains dogs, told me to be patient and to keep lessons short, no more than ten minutes a day. At first, Waffles just watched the ball roll away. After two weeks, he started chasing it, but he wouldn't bring it back. The trick, it turned out, was to swap: every time he dropped the ball, he got a tiny piece of cheese. Now he fetches so much that I'm the one who gets tired first!

questions.explain: 'He was scared of almost everything, even his own toys.'

train him for an hour a day

he still only watched the ball
he lost the ball in the garden

passages.title: Report: Our Visit to Blue Bay Aquarium
passages.text: On Tuesday, Year 6 visited Blue Bay Aquarium. The highlight for most of us was the tunnel, where sharks and rays swam right over our heads. A guide explained that the aquarium's sea turtles had all been rescued after getting caught in fishing nets; they will be returned to the ocean once they are strong enough. Later, we were allowed to touch a starfish, although we had to wash our hands first. The only disappointment was the penguin feeding, which had been cancelled because one penguin was unwell.

passages.title: The Girl Who Talked to Clouds
passages.text: In the village of Thistledown, it hadn't rained for three months, and the crops were dying. Everyone had tried something: the miller had danced, the baker had sung, and the queen had even promised a white pony to anyone who could bring rain. A quiet girl called Wren, who spent hours watching the sky, climbed the tallest hill and simply asked the clouds what was wrong. 'Nobody ever says thank you,' they grumbled. So the next morning, the whole village wrote thank-you notes and tied them to kites. By lunchtime, it was pouring.

questions.explain: 'It hadn't rained for three months, and the crops were dying.'

notes.she lived on a hill: She climbed the hill; she didn't live there.

questions.explain: 'Nobody ever says thank you.'

notes.people sang badly: The baker's singing isn't the reason.
notes.nobody looked at them: Wren looked at them a lot.

passages.title: Interview: The Young Chess Champion
passages.text: Twelve-year-old Ravi Kumar has just won the National Junior Chess Cup. We asked him a few questions. How did you start? 'My grandad taught me when I was six. I lost every game for a year!' How much do you practise? 'About an hour a day, but never on Sundays, because that's football day.' What's the hardest part? 'Staying calm. If I get nervous, I make silly mistakes.' What's next? 'I'd like to play in the world championship one day, but first I need to pass my maths test!'

passages.title: Ask the Space Expert
passages.text: Dear Space Expert, my brother says astronauts float because there's no gravity in space. Is he right? Amir, age 10. Dear Amir, it's a great question, but your brother isn't quite right. Gravity is still there in space; in fact, it's what keeps the Moon going round the Earth. Astronauts on the space station float because they are falling around the Earth all the time, together with the station. Since everything falls at the same speed, they feel weightless. It's a bit like the moment at the top of a roller coaster, but it lasts for months!

questions.explain: 'My brother says astronauts float because there's no gravity in space.'

passages.title: The Robot Football Tournament
passages.text: Last Saturday, twelve schools brought robots they had built themselves to the Robot Football Tournament. Each robot had to be smaller than a shoebox and was controlled by a tablet. Our robot, Kicky, was knocked out in the first round because its battery died after only three minutes. We were disappointed, but the judges gave us the 'Best Design' award because Kicky could change direction faster than any other robot. Next year we're definitely bringing a spare battery!

passages.title: Camping in the Storm
passages.text: Our family had planned to camp by the lake for three nights, but on the second evening a storm arrived. The wind was so strong that it bent one of our tent poles. While Dad was trying to fix it, my little sister noticed that the farmer next to the campsite had left his barn door open. He kindly let us sleep in the barn, which smelled of hay and was surprisingly cosy. In the morning, we woke up to find three curious goats staring at us. We went home a day early, but it's the trip we talk about most.

passages.title: Why Do Leaves Change Colour?
passages.text: In autumn, many trees turn from green to bright red, orange and yellow. Leaves are green because they contain chlorophyll, which helps trees make food from sunlight. When the days get shorter and colder, trees stop making chlorophyll to save energy for winter. As the green disappears, other colours that were hidden in the leaf all summer can finally be seen. Some red colours, however, are actually made in autumn, especially when there are sunny days and cool nights.

questions.explain: 'Chlorophyll, which helps trees make food from sunlight.'

passages.title: The Secret of the Old Clock Tower
passages.text: Nobody in Marlow had heard the old clock tower ring for fifty years. When Tom and his best friend Ada found a rusty key in the school garden, they guessed it might open the tower's door. They were right. Inside, they discovered that a family of owls had built a nest in the bell, which was why it couldn't ring. Instead of moving the owls, the town decided to build them a new home nearby. The bell was finally repaired last spring, and now it rings every hour, except at night, so the owls can hunt in peace.
